FR.name: France
FR.terroir_vibe: The spiritual home of fine wine, defined by the concept of AOC and strict adherence to traditional terroir.

IT.name: Italy
IT.terroir_vibe: An ancient mosaic of indigenous varietals and alpine-to-coastal climates. Balance and acidity are key.

ES.name: Spain
ES.terroir_vibe: High-altitude plateaus and Atlantic influence. Spain leads the world in organic vineyard area.

US.name: USA
US.terroir_vibe: Diversity from Pacific cooling to volcanic soils. A powerhouse of innovation and single-vineyard precision.

AR.name: Argentina
AR.terroir_vibe: High-altitude desert viticulture. Intense Andean sun creates concentrated, fruit-forward wines.

CL.name: Chile
CL.terroir_vibe: A climate island protected by the Andes and the Pacific. Famous for its phylloxera-free own-rooted vines.

ZA.name: South Africa
ZA.terroir_vibe: Ancient granite soils meet cold Atlantic breezes. A bridge between Old World structure and New World fruit.

AU.name: Australia
AU.terroir_vibe: From ancient iron-rich soils to cool maritime climates. Shiraz is the national icon.

NZ.name: New Zealand
NZ.terroir_vibe: Cool climate and intense UV light create vibrant, aromatic profiles. The benchmark for Sauvignon Blanc.

DE.name: Germany
DE.terroir_vibe: Steep slate slopes and river reflections. The world's most elegant expressions of Riesling.

PT.name: Portugal
PT.terroir_vibe: A treasure trove of unique indigenous grapes. Famous for Port but rapidly becoming a dry wine destination.

AT.name: Austria
AT.terroir_vibe: Strict quality standards and extreme focus on sustainable viticulture. Mineral-driven and structured.

GR.name: Greece
GR.terroir_vibe: Volcanic soils and sea mist. Home to some of the world's most resilient and unique ancient grapes.

GE.name: Georgia
GE.terroir_vibe: The birthplace of wine. Famous for Qvevri (clay vessel) fermentation and 8,000 years of history.

HU.name: Hungary
HU.terroir_vibe: Volcanic hills and noble rot. The Tokaj region produces some of the world's finest dessert wines.

IL.name: Israel
IL.terroir_vibe: Ancient tradition meets modern tech. High-altitude vineyards in the Judean hills are producing world-class reds.

LB.name: Lebanon
LB.terroir_vibe: High-altitude plateau with 300 days of sun. A tiny but mighty producer with deep French influences.

CN.name: China
CN.terroir_vibe: The world's fastest-growing wine region. Ningxia's desert conditions produce powerful, Cabernet-style reds.

CA.name: Canada
CA.terroir_vibe: Extreme continental climate. Famous for Icewine but increasingly celebrated for elegant cool-climate reds.

MD.name: Moldova
MD.terroir_vibe: The highest density of vineyards per capita in the world. Deep limestone cellars and rich black soil.

RO.name: Romania
RO.terroir_vibe: A massive producer with high-quality karst limestone soils, echoing the terroir of Burgundy.

HR.name: Croatia
HR.terroir_vibe: The original home of Zinfandel (Crljenak Kaštelanski). Dramatic limestone cliffs overlooking the Adriatic.

SI.name: Slovenia
SI.terroir_vibe: The land of 'Orange Wine'. A leader in natural winemaking with high-altitude alpine influences.

CH.name: Switzerland
CH.terroir_vibe: Steep terraced vineyards and glacial influence. Almost all Swiss wine is consumed domestically.

UY.name: Uruguay
UY.terroir_vibe: Atlantic-influenced maritime climate. Tannat is the national grape, known for its structure and health benefits.

MX.name: Mexico
MX.terroir_vibe: North America's oldest wine region. Arid Mediterranean climate tempered by Pacific cooling breezes.

BR.name: Brazil
BR.terroir_vibe: The capital of South American sparkling wine. Basalt soils and high humidity create fresh, vibrant profiles.

TR.name: Turkey
TR.terroir_vibe: Over 800 indigenous grape varieties. A bridge between ancient civilization and modern quality.

MA.name: Morocco
MA.terroir_vibe: High-altitude vineyards in the Atlas Mountains. Surprisingly fresh, Mediterranean-style reds.

JP.name: Japan
JP.terroir_vibe: Volcanic soils and high rainfall. Koshu produces delicate, floral whites that pair perfectly with sushi.

LB.name: Lebanon
LB.terroir_vibe: High altitude vineyards with 300 days of sun. A tiny but mighty producer with deep French influences.

AM.name: Armenia
AM.terroir_vibe: High-altitude volcanic soils. Home to the world's oldest known winery (Areni-1 cave).

CY.name: Cyprus
CY.terroir_vibe: Famous for Commandaria, the oldest named wine still in production. Phylloxera-free island.

BG.name: Bulgaria
BG.terroir_vibe: A historic producer with a focus on powerful, deep-colored reds from indigenous varietals.

RS.name: Serbia
RS.terroir_vibe: Resurgent tradition with a focus on Prokupac. Dramatic river-influenced microclimates.

PE.name: Peru
PE.terroir_vibe: Desert viticulture influenced by the Humboldt Current. Famous for Pisco but increasingly producing fine dry wines.

CO.name: Colombia
CO.terroir_vibe: High-altitude tropical viticulture. Unique 'double harvest' cycle due to consistent equatorial conditions.

DO.name: Dominican Republic
DO.terroir_vibe: The only commercial vineyards in the Caribbean. Extreme tropical conditions produce unique, localized styles.
